title: The stone head
logline: A moss-grown carved face by a shingle wall, half sunk in grass. The concept sheet's landmark. Drawn from every side; this is the front.

panels.composition: A bench by a shingle wall near the water. Beside it, half sunk in grass: a carved stone head the size of a barrel, moss over the eyes, a broad calm face. WOOD on the bench with a mug, from three-quarters behind — we get the side of his face for the first time in the private work. BARNABY II asleep against the stone. The bird on the head's crown.

characters.pose: on the bench, three-quarters from behind

props: stone head, moss over the eyes

image.prompt: a man seen three-quarters from behind sitting on a bench with a mug beside a shingle wall, next to a large moss-grown carved stone head half sunk in grass with a calm broad face, a three-legged dog asleep against the stone, a small rainbow bird on the head's crown, spare ink and muted watercolor, no panel borders, no words
image.notes: The concept sheet's 'But Small Wood has its moments' bench. The head is never explained.

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards

notes: The stone head. Where it came from is reserved. The strip sits with it.
